narrative.text: Presents the opening section of WHO Summary Table 2 (updated December 2025) detailing minimum age of first dose, number of primary doses, inter-dose intervals, booster doses, and key considerations for universally recommended childhood vaccines: RSV (maternal vaccination or newborn monoclonal antibody), BCG, Hepatitis B, and Polio (bOPV+IPV preferred, early, hexavalent, sequential IPV/bOPV, and 3-dose or post-cessation 2-dose IPV-only schedules).

Continues WHO Summary Table 2 (updated December 2025) for universally recommended childhood vaccines, specifying minimum ages, primary series dose counts, intervals, and booster schedules for DTP-containing vaccines, Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib), Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (3p+0 and 2p+1 options), Rotavirus, Measles, Rubella, and HPV.

Completes WHO Summary Table 2 (updated December 2025) with childhood dosing schedules for regional, high-risk, and programme-specific vaccines—Japanese Encephalitis, Yellow Fever, Tick-Borne Encephalitis, Typhoid, Cholera, Meningococcal, Hepatitis A, Rabies, Dengue (TAK-003), Malaria, Mumps, Seasonal Influenza, Varicella, and the alternative 1p+1 PCV schedule—followed by comprehensive footnotes (1–24) detailing WHO position paper guidance for each antigen.

Provides the introductory header and disclaimer for WHO's December 2025 Summary Table 2 on recommended routine immunizations for children, noting that the cited ages and dose intervals are intended to guide country-specific schedule development based on local epidemiologic, programmatic, resource, and policy considerations.
